for_senior_author: Design and instrument, sc_karamouzian_2018: keep 'cross-sectional' (the authors' label; one record per visit, no follow-up). Its comparisons are by strip result and by stated intention, exposures that cannot be assigned, with no visits without a check to compare, so ROBINS-I has no intervention contrast to judge: the design-matched choice under §5.3 is ROBINS-E for those comparisons, with the JBI prevalence checklist for the uptake, positivity and intention figures most claims cite. Either is a new appraisal with a blind check (§5.6(c)); the overall judgment would carry over (critical to very high) and no claim's rating would change. The card keeps ROBINS-I for now.

Design and instrument, sc_klaire_2022: keep 'cross-sectional' (the authors' own description) and ROBINS-I, which fits its main comparison of two ways of delivering an intervention (take-home testing against on-site testing; §5.3: 'ROBINS-I for interventions'); it is not a test-accuracy study (no reference method, no paired samples). The mismatch is in scripts/rob_vocab.py, whose DESIGN_INSTRUMENT row for 'cross-sectional' lists only ROBINS-E and JBI: proposed editor's change, add ROBINS-I to that row so the table matches §5.3. The same question applies to sc_measham_2019 (filed 'case-series', for which §5.3 lists no instrument, but appraised with ROBINS-I): re-file as cross-sectional, or keep case-series without an instrument.
